boxes.comments: The tall crossed t and low ous run support tous. In the middle word the first low hump/cup, small following loop and terminal hook favor nos; the joined initial curve and loop leave ces possible. The b ascender, e/a bodies, low u and crossed final x support beaux. No neighboring word is completed.

The opening has e/x/t followed by a detached stop; abbreviation retained. Type has a descending y partly cut at the lower edge, but the central word is recoverable. Fini has the long f and two separate i dots. The final Q is a round body and tail, with no separately secured double-struck stroke. The trailing comma is visible.
Live ou is followed by a separate small circular 0 and a descending comma. This is an inline numeral, with no surrounding formula-label enclosure.

A faint sign to the left has two pale approximately horizontal components, the lower with darker middle bumps; literal equals remains tentative. Both U and V have separate overbars and a comma divides them. U has an open hooked upper-left entry and a rounded right-foot return. Clipped preceding text is not supplied.

Définissent is supported by d loop and ascender, initial accented e, long f, two i dots, compressed internal low strokes and final crossed t. Des has the d ascender, low e and terminal s hook. No detached punctuation is secured.

Capital E has a separate raised accent. The tall t strokes and their crossing lines belong to Étant; no independently secured cancellation is present. Donné has a looped d, o, two compressed n bodies and final e with a detached acute.

Poincaré ends in an accented e followed by a separate dark period. The following U has a curled/looped upper-left entry and broad right-foot return. Above it there is an upper wavy stroke and a lower shorter nearly horizontal return; the lower component may be a separate bar under a tilde or retracing within the tilde. Both accent-count readings remain local alternatives. No mathematical meaning is used to choose.

A separate horizontal strike crosses the entire recoverable telle, including the tall t and two l-like ascenders; no final s is secured. The following on is live. Its thin internal connector is not taken as continuation of the cancellation.

The central word has c/o/m/p/l, a low medial e, crossed t and final accented e. No separate acute is securely visible above the medial e; unaccented e is preferred there. One final accented e body is secure; a merged further terminal e cannot be excluded, so the ending remains local. The raised formula is read separately in B10 and B11.

The raised formula has an open hooked upper-left U entry and one angular hat. A long curved leader descends to the gap after the preceding baseline word. Its upper comma-like bend is continuous with the leader. A separate lower baseline comma remains outside the insertion. Both connector ends are visible in this box and in the permitted original. A clipped trace from the line above is not completed.

This tighter overlapping box independently shows the raised open-entry U and its single angular hat. It excludes the baseline comma and most of the attachment leader, so those are not supplied in this row. Insertion state is visible in B10 and the original. Clipped neighboring traces are omitted.

The initial abbreviation has two tall joined t-like strokes and a crossbar. The following faded word has an initial small a-like loop, a faint low run, a tall t, a round low o and low terminal humps, favoring autom without expansion. Its internal faint strokes remain tentative. The detached terminal mark has a rounded dark head and a downward curl; stop versus comma remains unresolved.

Both enclosing parentheses and the separating comma are present. The first U has a pronounced curled oval upper-left entry and a broad right-foot return. Its heavy upper mark rises, dips and rises again, favoring a tilde; a retraced bar remains possible. The K has distinct angled arms and a separate approximately straight overbar. The adjacent clipped trace at the top is not completed.

The parenthesis and final l’identité are visible. The first group has a long looped descending initial stroke, faint middle curves and a dotted short ending, favoring qui, but the pale strokes remain tentative. The next group has a short initial stem, faint low n-like run, tall looped d, low u, dot and final tall crossed/angled t, favoring induit. A small dark trace after the first group is not secured as independent punctuation. Upper neighboring fragments and the lower clipped formula are excluded. The final accent and ending are faint but included in the central identity word.

Induit shows an initial dotted i, a faint n connector, looped d, low u, another i dot and final t. Un follows. Endom. retains the source abbreviation and its separate terminal stop. Final de has a looped d and low e. Fragments at the top edge are excluded.

One angular hat sits over a U with a large oval curled upper-left entry and a broad lower cup/right upright. The letter is rendered calligraphically from that entry form. The final dark mark is a compact stop without a separately secured long comma tail. No further accent is supplied.
Separate lower-left marginal foliation 61: a closed lower loop and curved upper stroke form 6; a sloping entry and upright form 1. It is recorded as a margin number, not an autograph head number.

independence_attestation: Only the generic blind contract, assigned original scan, frozen coordinate list and fresh crops derived from that original were opened for this assignment. No witnesses, first readings, page transcriptions, packets, notes, reviews, notation tables, comparison files or other pages were opened. Every listed crop was visually read. No OCR or text-recognition software was used.
method: Original image viewed, then each frozen box cropped once from the original, enlarged to 2800 pixels wide with LANCZOS, autocontrasted and mildly sharpened using UnsharpMask radius 1.2, percent 110, threshold 3. No rotations were applied; the sloping lines remained readable in their source orientation. Existing saved crops were used for focused rereading. B12 was reopened after a display truncation prevented its first attempted view from being read.
return_policy: The TSV and metadata will remain unchanged after return; the main reader performs the later comparison and audit.
